why: Series Be honest. Adapts the gym humor mechanics that generate strong engagement (2-3k views on her profile) paired with a practical coaching takeaway.
rules:
Videos in English. Natalia = personal trainer, 41, mum of a 4-year-old, Singapore. Audience: women 35+, many mums.
FOOTAGE: only Natalia's own footage (her Google Drive / her reels). NEVER stock, NEVER strangers, NEVER other people's interviews or viral clips.
ONE topic per video; finish the thought logically. Technique videos: ONE exercise. Exception: follow-along workouts Natalia films herself (e.g. 4 shoulder moves with water bottles) are allowed - one topic, several moves. Never mix exercises that don't belong to one workout.
Only expert-grade technique content: cues must be correct and specific (e.g. ribs down, push through heels, pause at top). Weak or generic technique explanation = do not publish.
Hooks: from what goes viral now (technique of legs/glutes, strength for life 35+), concrete, no filler questions (no 'morning or evening', no 'how long is your quick rest').
Never repeat topics she already posted. Do not recycle hooks from her own old reels.
Every shot must match what is said at that moment. No random lifestyle shot as an ending (e.g. running on the field with her son) unless the line is about him.
Final CTA frame: Natalia looking directly into the camera saying the call to action. Video must not just cut off.
CTA: Comment "START".
Captions: same style in every video - big Montserrat ExtraBold italic, 1-2 words, white with lilac key words; hook plate at start, end card. Always white and lilac.
Voice: Natalia's real voice when she sends it; otherwise her ElevenLabs clone. Never robotic voice with unnatural pauses.
Never shame bodies, no before/after, never promise weight loss/results/health outcomes, no medical or nutrition claims. Never write 'free'.
Plus-size assistant (Strong Together): only strength and confidence, only with her consent, starts when footage exists.
Tone: warm, honest coach-mum, expert.
NO nudity or semi-nude shots (shower, bare back) - she declines them.
Name exercises exactly: underhand grip = chin-up (biceps + back), not pull-

problems: Audio talks about building muscle and strength training, but the footage is mostly lifestyle/kid on a toy car with no actual workout or training clips shown
Hook shows a static table shot of a kid eating breakfast, which does not immediately stop the thumb for a women's fitness coaching video
The toy car clip is repeated twice (0:03-0:05 and 0:07-0:08) with an awkward washed-out flash transition
qa.fix: Replace the repetitive toy car and breakfast clips with dynamic footage of Natalia actually strength training, showing muscle-building exercises that directly connect to the energy needed for motherhood.
